findings.summary: The recorded-timings exemption lets through the joined readings the check is meant to refuse.
findings.evidence: The plan exempts any reading whose title, summary or criteria contain 'recorded timings', 'already recorded' or 'shard-timings.txt'. HISTORY.txt shows commit 73f94d2 'Balance xtask test-shard by recorded per-target timings', which adds xtask/shard-timings.txt. That file is where a measurement stage writes its result. A joined reading such as 'time the full workspace test run, write the per-binary timings to xtask/shard-timings.txt, then fix the slowest binary chosen from the result' has all three signals, but the exemption still lets it through. Because has_phrase treats '-' as a word boundary, 'already-recorded timings' also matches 'recorded timings'. Any mention of past timings anywhere in the text therefore exempts the whole reading. Fix: Base the exemption on what the reading asks for, not on a file name being mentioned: a fix-only reading is accepted because it has no run signal, so it needs no exemption. Drop the 'shard-timings.txt' and 'already recorded' phrases. If an exemption is still needed, it should apply only when no criterion asks for a new full timed run. Add a corpus case and a unit test for a joined reading that names xtask/shard-timings.txt and is refused by check_measure_then_fix.
findings.location: Plan step 1 (exemption list) and Decision 3; xtask/shard-timings.txt in HISTORY.txt commit 73f94d2

findings.summary: The signals match text that describes the rule, so readings about the check itself (this job's reading included) would be refused.
findings.evidence: The signals match text that describes the measure-then-fix shape, not only text that schedules it. This job's own accepted reading shows the problem. Criterion 1 reads 'a reading whose request joins a full timed workspace test run with a fix chosen from its result is refused'. It contains 'full timed', 'timed', the whole word 'fix' and 'chosen from', so it hits all three signals. It escapes only because criterion 2 happens to contain 'recorded timings'. Once the exemption is fixed, this reading would be refused. So would the follow-up that open question 2 proposes (widening the phrase lists), and any future reading that edits or documents this rule. Fix: Add a unit test and a corpus case built from this job's reading text (title, summary and criteria verbatim), and show it is accepted. Then tighten the signals until that test passes and the joined cases are still refused. One option: count the run signal only in a criterion that tells someone to run and time the full suite. Another: take the fix signal from the reading's structure, for example code deliverables beyond the timings entry or a code/tests class of work, instead of the bare word 'fix'.
findings.location: Plan step 1 (signals over title, summary, criteria); Demonstration for criterion 1

findings.summary: The fix word 'optimi' and the bare word 'fix' miss their inflected forms under whole-word matching.
findings.evidence: has_phrase (reading.rs:3236) matches whole words only: it fails when the character after the match is alphanumeric. 'optimi' in 'optimise', 'optimize' or 'optimization' is followed by a letter, so it never matches. The same rule stops the whole word 'fix' from matching 'fixes', 'fixed' or 'fixing'. Fix: List the full word forms ('optimise', 'optimize', 'fixes', 'fixing', and so on), or use a stem match on purpose. Add a unit variant for each form.

findings.summary: Requiring three phrase lists to match together lets paraphrases through; a structural signal would hold better.
findings.evidence: All three phrase lists must match together. A reading that says 'time the full workspace test run; then speed up the slowest binary' has no phrase from the dependency list, so it passes. Open question 2 admits that a paraphrase gets through. The Reading struct already holds structural fields (deliverables, class_of_work, criterion kinds) that would show a fix stage more reliably than words like 'chosen from'. Fix: Consider replacing the dependency-phrase signal with a structural one: a criterion that asks for a new full timed run, plus deliverables that change code. Then the refusal does not depend on the reader's wording.

summary: The plan puts the fix in the right place: a new step! in refusing_check, which is where the combined shape gets through. The names it relies on exist: refusing_check, check_criteria_evidence, has_phrase, producer_evidence_phrase, reading_with_criterion, base_reading/request_text_acceptance, INPUT_FORMS [&str; 17], READING_RULES [&str; 6], the 2400-byte section bound, and the Unreleased/Changed section of CHANGELOG.md. Its demonstrations name real seams and would fail without the check. The heuristic itself has two problems. First, the exemption for 'shard-timings.txt' or 'recorded timings' lets through the very joined readings the check targets, because a measurement stage writes to xtask/shard-timings.txt. Second, the signals match text that describes the rule, so this job's own reading escapes only by luck through that exemption, and future work on the rule would be refused. Smaller issues: 'optimi' can never match under whole-word matching, and the dependency signal depends on wording where a structural signal from the reading's fields would be more reliable. Verdict: revise, so that the exemption is fixed and a test shows this job's own reading is accepted.
